title: 10 Non-Chordate Phyla, One Key Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Ten jars on the college museum shelf: a sponge, a jellyfish, a tapeworm, a starfish and six more, each from a different phylum. NEET asks about every one, so Diya asks: is there one key that can sort them all?

We open the jars one by one with labelled living diagrams: Porifera, Coelenterata, Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata and Hemichordata, each with its key feature and NCERT examples. Then an animated classification key sorts all ten jars, we compare the pairs students mix up, and run the key on a cuttlefish. Then the Hemichordata exam trap, an original match the following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 35 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Ten jars on the museum shelf
0:32 The ten phyla, one by one
2:41 The key that sorts all ten
3:25 Pairs that get mixed up + pause and think
4:06 Worked example: the cuttlefish jar
4:32 Exam trap: is Hemichordata a chordate?
4:56 Practice question (match the following)
5:19 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Chordate Characteristics. A fish embryo and a human embryo share a rod along the back: what else do they share?
